To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have calibrated the polarimeter P.O.M.M.E. in the energy range between 175 and 1600 MeV, using the deuteron beam of Saturne.
we measured the vector analyzing powers in a wide energy range for the reaction 12C(d,d′)12C, and we obtained empirical formulae that fit our results.
The calibration of POMME for the energy range 175–1800 MeV was carried out.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new calibration method for a polarimeter for the measurement of the vector and tensor analyzing powers for the inclusive scattering of deuterons by carbon.
the development of new polarimeters and with the study of the spin structure of nuclei.
the measurement of the vector analyzing power in the inclusive reaction of polarized deuterons on polarized protons at energies between 200 MeV and 1800 MeV.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present results for the analyzing powers are the best presently available in this energy range.
the present calibration is in agreement with the previous calibrations, but that it is more precise and that the energy range has been extended.
the present calibration is the most precise one available to date for energies between 1 and 1.4 GeV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the vector analyzing powers for deuteron energies below 0.7 GeV can be fitted as a function both of scattering angle and energy, with a relative error of less than 1% for the energy range between 1 and 3.5 GeV/c.
the present data and the corresponding analysis are a useful tool to study the reaction mechanism of deuteron breakup at energies between 1 and 2 GeV, and to test the validity of different models.
the analyzing powers for the reaction d+C→X, in a wide range of energies and scattering angles, are now available for the first time, with an accuracy of 5–10%.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the vector analyzing powers are very sensitive to the energy dependence of the nuclear potential, which can be used to constrain the nuclear potential in the energy range between 1.2 and 1.4 GeV, where the vector analyzing powers show a pronounced energy dependence.
the analyzing powers are well described by simple functions of the energy and the scattering angle, and that the energy dependence can be described by a single function.
the energy and angular dependence of the vector analyzing powers can be described with high accuracy using simple formulae, with only a few parameters.
